Abdul El-Sayed

Democratic candidate for U.S. Senate, Michigan · Open seat

Physician and epidemiologist; former public health official

Abdul El-Sayed is a physician and former Detroit and Wayne County public health official. He won Michigan's August 2026 Democratic primary for U.S. Senate, defeating U.S. Rep. Haley Stevens. He is the Democratic nominee for the open seat in the November 3, 2026 general election.

Where El-Sayed stands

Health care
Supports Medicare for All and calls it his signature plan. Says he would expand Medicare to cover vision, dental and hearing care and extend it to everyone.
Cost of living / economy
Says he would work to lower the cost of living for Americans.
Israel / foreign aid
Campaigns on ending U.S. military aid to Israel.
Campaign finance
Campaigns on getting corporate money out of politics.
Iran
Said Iran has posed a threat to U.S. national security. Argues that the 2015 nuclear deal helped contain Iran through diplomacy.
